sources.title: Discrete-Time Signal Processing, 3rd Edition
sources.author: Alan V. Oppenheim and Ronald W. Schafer
sources.why: Canonical rigorous backbone for discrete-time LTI systems, convolution, DTFT/DFT, z-transforms, realizations, sampling, and FIR/IIR design; it anchors the mathematical derivations that the more intuitive sources deliberately streamline.

sources.title: Understanding Digital Signal Processing, 3rd Edition
sources.author: Richard G. Lyons
sources.why: Practicing-engineer companion for implementation intuition, FFT interpretation, FIR/IIR behavior, sample-rate conversion, finite-word formats, and debugging; its distinct role is turning the formal theory into field-ready mental models.

sources.title: Multirate Systems and Filter Banks
sources.author: P. P. Vaidyanathan
sources.why: Advanced capstone reference for decimation, interpolation, polyphase structures, noble identities, perfect-reconstruction filter banks, and paraunitary systems; it supplies depth beyond the introductory multirate treatments elsewhere in the canon.

sources.title: Introduction to Signal Processing
sources.author: Sophocles J. Orfanidis
sources.why: Primary legal open textbook for a complete computational pass through quantization, convolution, z-domain reasoning, realizations, FFT spectral analysis, FIR/IIR design, and sample-rate conversion, with C and MATLAB material.

sources.title: The Scientist and Engineer's Guide to Digital Signal Processing
sources.author: Steven W. Smith
sources.why: Pre-course and laboratory bridge that builds numerical intuition for arrays, convolution, Fourier analysis, recursion, filters, and applications before the learner meets the rigorous transform and pole-zero treatments.

sources.title: Signals and Systems, MIT 6.003, Fall 2011
sources.author: Dennis Freeman
sources.why: Opening prerequisite sequence for signals, complex exponentials, LTI models, impulse responses, convolution, frequency response, sampling, transforms, and poles/zeros, with a paced set of lectures and solved exercises.

sources.title: The Fourier Transform and Its Applications, EE 261
sources.author: Brad Osgood
sources.why: Focused mathematical bridge for Fourier-series/transform duality, convolution, sampling and interpolation, DFT indexing, FFT, and zero padding; it gives transform conventions and the sampling theorem room that broad DSP texts cannot.

sources.title: Discrete-Time Signal Processing, MIT 6.341, Fall 2005
sources.author: Alan V. Oppenheim
sources.why: Main rigorous course spine after signals and systems, organizing structures, DFT/FFT, FIR/IIR design, short-time analysis, filter banks, and multirate processing into a tested lecture order with problems and exams.

sources.title: Spectral Analysis of Signals
sources.author: Petre Stoica and Randolph Moses
sources.why: Dedicated stochastic spectral-estimation source for random-process spectra, periodograms, nonparametric estimators, AR/MA methods, line spectra, and resolution-variance tradeoffs, filling a statistical gap left by deterministic Fourier treatments.

sources.title: Spectral Audio Signal Processing
sources.author: Julius O. Smith III
sources.why: Computational spectral-processing source for zero padding, peak interpretation, Welch estimation, STFT/spectrograms, FFT convolution, overlap-add/save, and executable MATLAB/Octave workflows.

sources.title: On the Use of Windows for Harmonic Analysis with the Discrete Fourier Transform
sources.author: Fredric J. Harris
sources.why: Definitive concentrated reading on finite-record spectral leakage and window choice, including main-lobe width, sidelobes, scalloping loss, equivalent noise bandwidth, overlap, and weak-tone detection.

sources.title: An Algorithm for the Machine Calculation of Complex Fourier Series
sources.author: James W. Cooley and John W. Tukey
sources.why: Load-bearing original reading for the FFT lesson: it exposes the factorization, operation-count argument, and radix decomposition in the concise paper that made fast DFT computation foundational.

sources.title: Seeing Circles, Sines, and Signals: A Compact Primer on Digital Signal Processing
sources.author: Jack Schaedler
sources.why: Interactive visual and auditory supplement for complex exponentials, phasors, sampling, aliasing, and the DFT; its unique role is making the equations directly manipulable before formal derivation.

sources.title: System identification campaign - Skywalker X8 UAV
sources.author: Bogdan Løw-Hansen and Richard Hann; NTNU UAV Lab
sources.why: Supplemental CC0 Version 1.0 measured dataset for a reproducible module-one application using ordered elevator-command and longitudinal-response records with creator-designated training and validation maneuvers.
